# Summary of 1997 UK Manifesto

## Economic Policy

The document presents an economic vision centered on maintaining competitive advantages gained over the previous 18 years. Key priorities include controlling public spending to below 40% of national income, reducing the basic income tax rate to 20%, maintaining inflation below 2.5%, and moving toward a balanced budget. The manifesto emphasizes Britain's position as a low-tax, low-regulation economy that has attracted significant foreign investment, contrasting this with higher unemployment rates in continental Europe attributed to heavier regulatory burdens.

## Employment and Business

The manifesto opposes additional workplace regulations and a national minimum wage, arguing these destroy jobs. It promotes support for small businesses through corporation tax cuts, reduced business rates, and simplified regulations. Unemployment support includes requiring long-term benefit recipients to undertake community work projects.

## Family and Welfare Policy

Proposals include allowing families with caring responsibilities to transfer unused tax allowances between spouses (worth up to £900 annually). A new pension scheme would provide young workers with personal pension funds through national insurance rebates. Other measures include respite care programs for family carers and a partnership scheme for funding elderly care without depleting lifetime savings.

## Education

The document guarantees intervention in underperforming schools, supports publication of test results, emphasizes traditional teaching methods, and promotes school diversity including grammar schools and specialist institutions. Nursery vouchers would provide universal pre-school access.

## Healthcare

The National Health Service would receive guaranteed real-terms funding increases annually. Reforms include expanding GP fundholding, enabling broader services in local surgeries, and increasing medical training places.

## Law and Order

Proposals include mandatory minimum sentences for persistent offenders, expanded prison capacity, CCTV installation funding, and measures targeting juvenile crime including parental responsibility orders. Electronic monitoring and community projects feature prominently.

## Constitutional Matters

The manifesto defends the constitutional union, opposing devolution to regional assemblies. It supports evolutionary rather than revolutionary constitutional change and opposes proportional representation voting systems.

## European Relations

The approach emphasizes intergovernmental cooperation over federalization, maintaining national vetoes, protecting border controls, and rejecting the Social Chapter. On currency union, the position holds that joining would require a referendum, while expressing skepticism about meeting convergence criteria.

## Environment and Rural Issues

Priorities include protecting green belt land, directing development to previously-used sites, supporting countryside stewardship, and maintaining international environmental commitments including reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
